A_target.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]].
Then every ideal of $R$ is [[Definition:Finitely Generated Ideal|finitely generated]] {{iff}} $R$ satisfies the [[Definition:Ascending Chain Condition|ascending chain condition]] on ideals, and if so $R \sqbrk x$ is again [[Definition:Noetherian Ring|Noetherian]].

B_source.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Principal Ideal Domain|principal ideal domain]].
Then every [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideal]] of $R$ is of the form $\ideal a$ for some $a \in R$.

substitutions.the class of principal ideal domains: the wider class of Noetherian rings

derived.stabilization of ascending chains: the equivalent form of finite generation
derived.closure under polynomial extension: the Hilbert basis theorem, which has no principal analogue

object_map.reformulation: Relax generation by a single element to generation by finitely many, which is what closure under polynomial extension requires.

validity_conditions: Principal ideal domains are Noetherian, taking the single generator as the finite generating set, so the generalization is faithful.
The equivalence of finite generation with the ascending chain condition uses that the union of a chain of ideals is an ideal, generated by finitely many elements appearing at some finite stage.

The generalization is strictly necessary for the Hilbert basis theorem: a polynomial ring in two variables over a field is Noetherian but not a principal ideal domain, so the principal class is not closed under the construction.
proof_plan: Replace generation by one element with generation by finitely many.

Let $I_1 \subseteq I_2 \subseteq \cdots$ be a chain.
Then $I = \displaystyle \bigcup_k I_k$ is an ideal; if $I = \ideal {a_1, \ldots, a_m}$, all $a_j$ lie in some $I_N$, so the chain stabilizes.
Conversely, if some ideal is not finitely generated, adding generators one at a time gives a strictly ascending chain.
In a principal ideal domain every ideal is generated by one element, so PIDs are Noetherian.
